key_big: Physics explains motion, forces and energy around us.
body_html:
How to think about it

Physics is the study of matter, energy, motion and forces. We use it when we ride a jeepney, cook, use a cellphone or switch on a fan. Physicists measure quantities in SI units: meters, kilograms, seconds, amperes and kelvins.

Motion is described by distance and displacement, speed and velocity, and acceleration. Speed = distance ÷ time; acceleration is the change in velocity per second. Measuring carefully with the right instrument and units gives reliable results.

Example

A jeepney travels 30 km in 0.5 h. Average speed?

30 ÷ 0.5

Answer: 60 km/h

Example

Which SI unit measures mass?

Not grams

Answer: the kilogram

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up mass and weight.
  • Forgetting to convert minutes to seconds.
  • Mixing up distance and displacement.

faq.q: Why do we need SI units?
faq.a: So that measurements are the same and can be compared all over the world.

faq.q: Is a car going round a curve at constant speed accelerating?
faq.a: Yes, because its direction, and so its velocity, changes.

items.q: Which SI prefix stands for 10⁻¹²?
items.e: p (pico) stands for 10⁻¹².

items.q: What power of ten does the prefix m (milli) stand for?
items.e: m (milli) stands for 10⁻³.

items.q: Which SI prefix stands for 10⁶?
items.e: M (mega) stands for 10⁶.

items.q: The ampere (A) is the SI base unit of which quantity?

items.q: The mole (mol) is the SI base unit of which quantity?

items.q: What is the SI base unit of time?

items.q: Which SI prefix stands for 10³?
items.e: k (kilo) stands for 10³.

items.q: The kilogram (kg) is the SI base unit of which quantity?

items.q: What power of ten does the prefix c (centi) stand for?
items.e: c (centi) stands for 10⁻².

items.q: What power of ten does the prefix G (giga) stand for?

items.q: The meter (m) is the SI base unit of which quantity?

items.q: Which SI prefix stands for 10⁻³?

items.q: What power of ten does the prefix M (mega) stand for?

items.q: Which method is used to measure the distance of a nearby star?
items.e: The star seems to shift against distant stars as Earth moves round the Sun.

items.q: What is 12.11 + 18.0 + 1.012 written to correct decimal places?
items.e: In addition keep the least number of decimal places (one, from 18.0).

items.q: What is the dimensional formula of the gravitational constant G?
items.e: From F = Gm₁m₂/r², G = Fr²/(m₁m₂).

items.q: A formula is dimensionally correct. Does this prove it is correct?
c: no, but a dimensionally wrong formula must be wrong
items.e: Numbers and constants cannot be checked.

items.q: Which is the SI unit of solid angle?
items.e: Plane angle is in radians.

items.q: Which of these quantities has no dimensions?
items.e: Strain is a ratio of two lengths.

items.q: How many significant figures are there in 0.00087?
items.e: Leading zeros never count; zeros between digits and trailing zeros after a decimal point do. So 2.

items.q: What is 1 light year?
c: the distance light travels in one year
the time light takes to reach Earth
items.e: It is a unit of distance, about 9.46 × 10¹⁵ m.

items.q: Which atomic clock standard defines the second?
items.e: One second is 9 192 631 770 periods of a cesium radiation.

items.q: How many significant figures are there in 2.64 × 10²⁴?
items.e: Leading zeros never count; zeros between digits and trailing zeros after a decimal point do. So 3.

items.q: What is the result of 2.5 × 1.25 written to correct significant figures?
items.e: The answer keeps the fewest significant figures in the data (2).

items.q: Which is the correct way to write the SI unit of force?
items.e: Unit symbols are not capitalized in words and take no full stop.

items.q: How many significant figures are there in 0.007?
items.e: Leading zeros never count; zeros between digits and trailing zeros after a decimal point do. So 1.

items.q: How many significant figures are there in 3.0 × 10⁸?
items.e: Leading zeros never count; zeros between digits and trailing zeros after a decimal point do. So 2.

items.q: Which kind of error is caused by a zero error in an instrument?
c: a gross error of reading the wrong scale
items.e: It shifts every reading in the same direction.

items.q: How many significant figures are there in 0.00305?

items.q: How many base units are there in the SI system?

items.q: A bike slows from 22 m/s to 10 m/s in 3 s. What is its acceleration?
items.e: a = (10 − 22) ÷ 3 = −4 m/s² (slowing down).

items.q: What does Newton's third law state?
c: momentum is always lost in collisions
if An exerts a force on B, B exerts an equal and opposite force on A
an object at rest stays at rest
items.e: The pair act on different objects.

items.q: What does Newton's second law state?
c: objects keep moving unless a force acts
the resultant force equals mass times acceleration, F = ma
items.e: Acceleration is in the direction of the resultant force.

items.q: What does the slope of a velocity–time graph give?
items.e: Slope = Δv/Δt.

items.q: A runner covers 125 m in 25 s and then 120 m in 15 s. What is the average speed?
items.e: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 245 ÷ 40 = 6.12 m/s.

items.q: What does the area under a velocity–time graph give?
items.e: Area = velocity × time.

items.q: A boy runs round a circular track of length 1,000 m and comes back to the start in 130 s. What is his average velocity?
items.e: Displacement is zero, so average velocity is 0; average speed is 7.69 m/s.

items.q: What does the gradient of a velocity–time graph give?
items.e: The area under it gives displacement.

items.q: What is momentum?
items.e: Unit kg m/s.

items.q: A bike slows from 30 m/s to 0 m/s in 6 s. What is its acceleration?
items.e: a = (0 − 30) ÷ 6 = −5 m/s² (slowing down).

items.q: A car's speedometer reads 60 km/h. What does it show?
items.e: It shows speed at that moment.

items.q: What is terminal velocity?
c: the constant speed reached when air resistance balances weight
the speed when an object hits the ground
